highlight.title: Netflix's $1.52 Trillion Technical Debt Story
highlight.summary: Netflix's journey from a 2008 outage to running 1,000+ microservices shows how architectural decisions shape business success. Their migration from monolithic to microservices architecture eliminated single points of failure and enabled handling 15x traffic spikes while reducing costs by 30%.

resources.title: Software Architecture: The Complete Beginner's Guide
resources.why_now: <cite index="26-4,26-13">This guide provides clear starting points for understanding software architecture basics, making systems easier to scale, secure, test, and maintain</cite>. Perfect for curious adults who want to understand how software systems work without getting lost in technical jargon.

resources.title: SOLID Principles with Real-World Examples
resources.why_now: <cite index="32-21,32-22">SOLID principles help write code that's easier to maintain, test, and extend as projects grow, with better separation of concerns</cite>. These timeless principles apply whether you're building a simple app or Netflix-scale systems.

resources.title: Netflix Architecture Case Study: Building for 300M Users
resources.why_now: <cite index="11-5,11-8">Netflix serves over 300 million subscribers across 190+ countries, handling billions of viewing hours monthly and more than a trillion events per day</cite>. Their architectural decisions offer battle-tested lessons for any growing system.

resources.title: Software Architecture Patterns That Scale in 2026
resources.why_now: <cite index="2-19,2-20">The right pattern depends on your specific situation: team size, growth trajectory, deployment constraints, and business timeline</cite>. This guide helps experienced engineers choose architecture patterns based on actual needs, not trends.

claude_take: <cite index="3-19">Technical debt from poor architecture has grown to $1.52 trillion impact on the U.S. economy, highlighting why choosing the right architectural pattern early is critical</cite>. The gap between "working code" and "maintainable systems" has never been more expensive to ignore, making architectural literacy essential for everyone in tech.
